title: How the second Label X album came about
summary: Jerry Brightman set it up after Handy took over a date, and he designed a one-of-each band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: How did that come about?
The writing of that album?
Yeah, who asked for what?
This was for Label X and it was through Jerry Brightman, the same guy that didn't do too well for me in some situations, and did very well for me in other situations.
He was still considered a friend?
He was always a friend, even when he stole from me, even during the years of hating, because I remember the beginnings with
Is he still around?
Well I heard of him last year; I don't recall what he was into, trying to promote something or other.
We were talking about? The second album.

The album. Well, we had--Jerry had set up the thing with Label X with a guy named Jimmy Hilliard that represented the company. They were a subsidiary of RCA Victor, and Jimmy Hilliard had originally booked an all star jazz date under the director--I can't think of the other musician--it was supposed to be the front, under his leadership, and I was to contribute some of the charts and he was going to do the other charts.

So about a day or two before the date, they notified me that he backed out of the date and they would like me to take over the date completely and write the other four things--I don't remember how many--write the things that
How long did it take you to write that date?
Not too long. It was done very quickly.
Days? Weeks?
A few days. All I had to do was write heads and closings, everything in between was free blowing.
Heads and closings are terribly sophisticated. That's a personal opinion.
I never felt pleased by that album, there are things in it that I don't enjoy, there are things that I do enjoy.
Excuse me, are you referring to Handyland?
Yeah.
Oh, I thought we were on the second album.
Oh, we're talking about the second album; right.

Well, I was telling you how the second album came about. Through the first album, which originally was supposed to be someone else's--his name escapes me--the guy that backed out--and as a result of my taking over the first album, they offered me a second one; write anything you want. I said, well, I want to do some experimental work; is that all right with you, creating some new jazz forms, and they said go ahead.

So I conceived of an orchestra of one each, only in the sense that I had one violin, each with a chair, one flute, one trumpet, one trombone, one alto, one tenor, one baritone, bass, piano, drum. I was fortunate in knowing Gene Orloff who plays violin beautifully, who plays trumpet beautifully, so although he was the originally conceived violinist for the date, I
also had the use of his trumpet, which gave me three brass where I wanted it. I just took him off the violin.
So the violin chair had a trumpet and it gave me an extra horn too. And then there were various doublings throughout the band.
